messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: doc and chained_var_context
parts:
All the new services doc needs a lot of work. What we want
to do for class doc is say what the object does and optionally
provide the use case. So instead of

A chained_var_context object represents two objects
of var_context as one.

the doc should say how it represents two objects as one.

In particular, it should mention that the representation is
asymmetric, with a primary context and a secondary context, and
the set of defined variables is the union of the two names, but
if there's a conflict in that both define a variable, then the
primary's definition is used. (If they have to agree on names
defined both places, then that condition should be checked instead.)

Also, it doesn't appear to be correct in that I'd expect names_r
to be a set; as is, it's a vector that can allow names to show
up twice if they're defined in both var_contexts.

- Bob

worse, untested code in Stan at the moment.

If you're willing to help, mind starting with
the math library? I'd like to start making things
solid from the ground up and it's also easier to
work there and it's in less flux, so less chance of
doing a bunch of work for nothing.

You can pack as much into a doc issue as is practical
in order to not let things linger before a pull request.

Thanks.
